title: Records, Enums and Sealed Types
summary: Modern Java data modelling - records with compact constructors and value equality, enums with fields, methods and switch, EnumMap, sealed interfaces that list their implementations, and pattern matching in switch with record patterns for exhaustive handling of every case.

cards.q: What does `record Point(int x, int y) { }` give you?
cards.a:
Private final fields, a constructor, accessors `x()` and `y()`, and value-based `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString`

A record generates all of that from its components. The accessors are named after the components (`x()`, not `getX()`), and the fields are final, so a record is immutable.

cards.q: Why can a `switch` over a sealed interface leave out `default`?
cards.a:
The compiler knows every permitted subtype, so it can check that all are handled

The `permits` list names every possible subtype, so the compiler can prove the switch is exhaustive, and it stops compiling when a new subtype is added but not handled.

cards.q: Which is the best type for the four card suits?
cards.a:
An enum `Suit { HEARTS, DIAMONDS, CLUBS, SPADES }`

An enum gives a fixed, type-checked set of values, and a `switch` over it can be checked for completeness. Ints, strings and records all allow invalid values.
